name: momentum-weak
description: T-022 operator packet, run B of two: the SAME build and the SAME URL (index.html?momentum=1) played BADLY, so the pair differ only in how they are played. The policy is a player who has not learned the game yet — it only moves when the damage plane crowds it (edgeMargin<12), never aims up, and jumps only at the lip it is about to walk off. That keeps RIG on the LEFT of the screen, where decisions.md entry 11's daylight bank is empty: below CONFIG.momentum.bankLo (0.55 of the strip) the bank term is EXACTLY zero, so the only escalation left to a struggling player is the combat term, and its whole authority is wCombat = 0.3 of the range. FALSIFYING GATE, stated in what the code guarantees rather than in a raw speed: read `pursuitSpeed` out of `report.json` -> `trace` (the per-sample array; the report has no `samples` key) and convert with drive = (pursuitSpeed/4.3 - 1)/0.4. (1) If drive ever exceeds 0.30 — pursuitSpeed above 4.82 t/s, x1.12 — the bank deadband leaked and a player being carried was escalated at on daylight he never banked: the floor promise is broken and the task is not done. (2) After a hit, drive must be at or below hitDrive 0.35 (4.90 t/s) on the frame it lands and must not rise again for hitMercyMs 1500. (3) After a lost life the trace must return to exactly 4.30. Every constant in those three gates is checkable in src/config.js's momentum block. Escalation from KILLS inside that x1.12 bound is design-correct, not a failure — the combat term is independent of the bank by design, so a struggling player who holds fire and connects will read slightly above the floor. READ THE STRUCTURAL GAP, NOT THE DECIMALS (I-029). What reproduces is structural, and the only COMMITTED measurement of it is the T-022 gate's, in reports/tasks/T-022/playtest.md sections 2 and 4: this policy never once crossed the x1.12 bound (aboveX1.12 = 0 in both flag-on runs); flag ON and flag OFF are indistinguishable in outcome (maxX 59.6, maxScroll 75.0, 3 lives spent in all four runs), so escalation does not shorten a struggling run; and the strong/weak separation is 12-13x in the fraction of PLAYING samples above the shipped pace (0.7% / 11.6% here against 60.8% / 80.2% there). TWO RUNS PER SIDE IS A SAMPLE, NOT A BASELINE: the builder's own pair and the gate's landed outside several of each other's bands (section 10, and I-029 in SPRINT.md), and the run directories both were read from (tools/playtest/runs/gate-T-022-*) are gitignored and are not in the tree — so the per-run percentages and GAME_OVER times this description used to quote have been dropped rather than restated. Run it as: --deterministic, 1440x900, `--max-runtime-ms 62000` (the 60 s window needs that cap raised off its 25000 ms default). The 'pushed along while they learn' half is only PARTLY demonstrated here: RIG is conveyed forward to 75 m of scroll and then spends his last life well inside the window. This run shows the pace never escalated at a player who was losing; it does NOT by itself show that a struggling player can finish — no bot has ever finished the six-face run (docs/playtests/2026-08-victory-box.md).
